title: Build and run from a clean clone on Linux with GCC 15, without root
body: **What changes.** Three changes so that a clean clone reaches the compiler on Linux with GCC 15: the vendored zlib and libtiff are staged on Linux as `build-deps.ps1` already stages them on Windows, the vendored `tiffconf.h` takes its signed size type from the host instead of from `_WIN64`, and the remaining GCC 15 work is done from a clean clone without root. Seven files in all. What a clean clone reaches on Linux, as published and with the three branches. One bar per build step, stopping where the step stops.] **Why.** As published, `cmake` configure exits 1 and the compiler is never reached, so none of the seven executables the README's own table names can be built on this platform at all. **That nothing of yours is duplicated.** Two of the five branches we had are withdrawn here in favour of work already open: #14 by tesinclair, which is the same one line remedy we had for the gcc14+ implicit declarations, and #12 by TAUIL-Abd-Elilah, which is a better fix than ours for the Clipper2 ABI. Only the three that nobody has proposed are in this pull request. **What it is worth**, one row per branch, measured from a clean clone on Ubuntu with GCC 15, no root, 24 cores: | branch | files, lines | what it unblocks | |---|---|---| | `build-deps-stage-vendored-tiff` | 3 files, 57 added | the CMake path finds the vendored headers | | `vendored-tiffconf-host-width` | 1 file, 7 added, 2 removed | the TIFF reader sizes its offsets at the host's width | | `linux-build-audit-2026-09` | 3 files, 108 added, 13 removed | configure reaches the compiler | With all five of our branches the build is exit 0 in 30 s, all seven named executables plus three diagnostic tools, a shared library and three test binaries are produced, `ctest` is 3 of 3 passed and the shipped common suite is 23 of 23. **The three alone are necessary and not sufficient**: applied to `main` on their own they take `build-deps.sh` and configure to exit 0 and then the build stops at exit 1 in 25 s, on `implicit declaration of 'free'` at `src/api/scrollfiesta_api.c:1721`, which is exactly what #14 fixes. You need both. **How to check it yourself.** Clone `main`, apply these three, run `build-deps.sh` then `cmake` configure and `cmake --build`. Configure passes and the build stops where #14 applies. Apply #14 on top and it completes. --- On a Linux machine with GCC 15 the repository as published does not reach the compiler from a clean clone. This carries the three changes that are needed and are not already proposed, and cites the two open pull requests that cover the rest. ## What is already yours, and is not in here - **#14 by tesinclair** fixes the gcc14+ implicit declarations in `scrollfiesta_api.c` and `sf_pipeline.c`. We hit the same fault and had the same one line remedy on a branch of our own. **It is not in this pull request**: yours is open and it is the same fix. - **#12 by TAUIL-Abd-Elilah** standardises every build path on the non Z Clipper2 ABI, with a compile time guard and a regression over a strict square union and a 17 point self crossing boundary. We hit the same heap overflow through `Clipper2_union` during hole filling and our branch only stopped the two archives being linked into one binary. **Theirs is the better fix and this pull request does not compete with it.** That leaves three changes. ## 1. Stage the vendored zlib and libtiff on Linux `build-deps.ps1` stages them on Windows and nothing does on Linux, so the CMake path looks for headers that were never put where it expects. Three files, 57 lines added. ## 2. Take the vendored libtiff's signed size type from the host, not from `_WIN64` `tiffconf.h` as vendored decides the signed size type from `_WIN64`, which on a 64 bit Linux build selects the wrong width and the TIFF reader mis-sizes its offsets. One file, 7 lines added and 2 removed. ## 3. The remaining GCC 15 work, from a clean clone, without root Three files, 108 lines added and 13 removed. It is the difference between a checkout that stops at configure and one that produces every tool the README's own table names. ## What it is measured against From a clean clone on Ubuntu with GCC 15, no root, on a 24 core machine: | | with these branches | without them | |---|---|---| | `cmake` configure | exit 0 | **exit 1, the compiler is never reached** | | `cmake --build` | exit 0 in 30 s | not reached | | executables the README's table names | **all seven**, plus three diagnostic tools, a shared library and three test binaries | none | | the ten tools start and print their usage | yes | not reached | | `ctest` | **3 of 3 registered, 3 passed, 0 failed** | not reached | | the shipped common suite's own tally | **23 of 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** | not reached | The Makefile's `test` target does not run the suite on this machine; the CMake path is the repository's build of record and is what the table above is from. **That table was measured on a tree carrying all five of our branches**, including the two we have withdrawn above in favour of #14 and #12. So it is evidence that the five together build and test clean on Linux, and it is not evidence about the three alone. We said we would run the gate on the three and say what it gave. We have, and it is worth your time: | the three alone, on a tree exported from `main` | | |---|---| | the three apply to `main` | cleanly, with `git apply`, which takes no fuzz | | `build-deps.sh` | exit 0 in 12 s | | `cmake` configure | exit 0 in 1 s | | `cmake --build` | **exit 1 in 25 s**, after `libscrollfiesta_core.a` and `libsf_triangle.a` are built | | where it stops | one error: `implicit declaration of 'free'` at `src/api/scrollfiesta_api.c:1721` | **One word about the Makefile path, because the three changes have to agree with each other.** `build-deps.sh` stages the vendored zlib and libtiff into `deps/prefix`, so `src/Makefile` looks for them there: `TIFF_A` wildcards `../deps/prefix/lib/libtiff.a` and picks up `libz.a` from the same prefix, which a static libtiff needs. Where nothing has been staged it falls back to `-ltiff`, the system library, exactly as before. We mention it because an earlier draft of these changes had the staging in one place and the Makefile looking in another, which builds and links the system libtiff while appearing to use the vendored one. On this branch `make -n` puts `../deps/prefix/lib/libtiff.a` on the link line and no `-ltiff` at all. **Our three get you as far as configure and no further, and what stops the build is exactly what #14 fixes.** That was our expectation and it is now a measurement. The three are necessary and they are not sufficient; #14 is the other half, and on a Linux build of this repository today you need both. **One more thing a maintainer will want before merging.** With the three applied to `main`, #14 applies cleanly, both files. **#12 applies seven of its eight files and is rejected on one hunk, `src/Makefile:27`** , which is the same block of compiler flags our third change rewrites. Nothing about either change is wrong: they touch the same eighteen lines and whoever merges them resolves that hunk. We would rather you heard it from us than from the merge. ## One thing we noticed while reading #14 Its author writes that the same fix went in through #7 and is no longer in `main` or in the history, and wonders whether the public repository is periodically overwritten from a private one. We cannot see that from outside, but it would explain why a Linux build breaks again after being fixed, and it is worth saying out loud: if the public tree is a periodic export, a merged fix does not stay merged, and contributors will keep sending the same patch.
